title: Low-Cal Green Veggie Bibimbap
subtitle: with Sesame Pickled Cucumber
description: Think eating light means eating boring? Not in our book! Our low-cal recipes have all the punchy flavour and excitement you’d expect from us, and just 450 to 599 calories per serve.

steps.text: Cook rice: Fill a medium saucepan three-quarters full with water and bring to the boil. Add the rice and cook for 25-27 mins until tender. Drain. Meanwhile, thinly slice the cucumber. Thinly slice the broccoli stem and cut the head into small florets. Trim the stems from the snow peas, removing the strings from one side. Thinly slice the cabbage with a sharp knife or mandoline.
Pickle cucumber: Combine 2 tsp white vinegar and 1 tsp honey in a bowl and season with salt. Add the cucumber and toss to combine. Set aside to pickle, tossing occasionally, until needed.

Stir-fry greens: Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in a medium deep frypan over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the broccoli for 3-4 mins until slightly softened. Add the snow peas and 1 tbs water and stir-fry for a further 2 mins or until the veggies are just tender. Add the chilli paste (see Make it milder) and 1 tsp soy sauce and stir-fry for 30 secs. Remove the pan from the heat.

Fry eggs: Heat 1 tsp vegetable oil in a medium frypan over medium heat. Crack 2 eggs into the pan and cook for 3-4 mins until just set or cooked to your liking. Meanwhile, drain the cucumber, reserving the pickling liquid. Return the cucumber to the bowl, add half the sesame seeds and toss to combine.

Serve up: Combine the reserved pickling liquid and 1 tsp vegetable oil in a large bowl and season with salt and pepper. Add the cabbage and toss to coat. Divide the rice, stir-fried greens, cabbage and pickled cucumber among bowls. Top with the eggs, scatter over the remaining sesame seeds and enjoy!

Make it milder: Korean chilli paste, also known as gochujang, is a staple in every Korean pantry. It is slightly sweet, earthy and has a chilli kick. We've suggested this amount for flavour, but feel free to reduce to taste if you prefer less heat.
